items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: He's a clarinet player. He's a playing musician today. Dillard Rhodes. He has a shooter tying place like that.

ctx.x: Yeah. And I remembered, I remembered those arias from that time. And all I did was sing them and jot them down because usually when I do any writing, very seldom I use the piano. I use my solfege, you know, in writing the intervals, you know. Just do it by, in your head then. Yeah. And so I picked the chorus. Now I picked it very nice. And what was nice about it, the boys all liked it. I put a clarinet variation. I put a clarinet variation that this fellow around the corner on Claymore Street, you know him. He's…
Yeah. And I know him. Well. Well, do you know him?
